short: Audio-only decoder pre-training (M03) is standard after TTS decoder transfer; it lowers WER in 7 of 16 pairs, earlier systems keep lower WER, and no equal-training control or listener test exists.
position: The paper changes training (M03): it pre-trains the speech decoder on 3,572 hours of audio alone and transfers it to video-to-speech models. The design is standard: transferring a decoder trained without the input signal is used at least since 2021, and the paper's departure is dropping the transcripts a text-to-speech decoder needs. The transfer does not reliably help: it lowers WER against the same model trained from scratch in 7 of 16 model and split pairs and raises it in 9. Earlier systems keep lower WER on all four splits. The strongest confound is unequal training, since only pre-trained variants inherit a fully trained audio model, and every row is a single run with no listener test, so the claim that audio pre-training improves video-to-speech is not supported.
